knowledge-base.overview: Laravel 11+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices. Covers Eloquent ORM, Blade templates, Form Request validation, thin controllers, service layer, queues, routing, middleware, migrations, and testing with PHPUnit/Pest. Applies to PHP 8.2+ Laravel projects including full-stack web apps, APIs, and SaaS platforms.

core-principles.principle: Follow Laravel conventions for file placement, naming, and structure. Use artisan generators as the canonical way to scaffold classes.
Keep controllers thin. Extract all business logic into service classes. Controllers only handle HTTP concerns: receive input, call service, return response.
Validate all input through dedicated Form Request classes. Never validate in controllers or models.
Use ->with() or ->load() for relationships to prevent N+1 queries. Always think about query count before shipping a feature.
Offload email, notifications, PDF generation, and any operation exceeding 200ms to queued jobs.

guardrail.rule: Never use DB::raw() without parameter binding. Always use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.
Use $fillable (whitelist) on every Eloquent model. Never use $guarded = [] which allows mass-assignment of any column.
Escape Blade output with {{ }} (auto-escaped). Only use {!! !!} for trusted, pre-sanitized HTML. Never echo unsanitized user input.
Use declare(strict_types=1) at the top of every PHP file. Add typed properties and return types on all methods.
guardrail.good:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Services;

class PostService
{
    public function create(array $data): Post { /* ... */ }
}

guardrail.rule: Always eager load relationships. Never access relationships in loops without ->with(). Use ->paginate() or ->cursorPaginate() for list endpoints.
Use constructor property promotion with readonly for dependency injection in controllers and services.
Use Sanctum for API authentication. Never roll custom token authentication.
Always include down() in migrations for rollback. Never modify a deployed migration — create a new one instead.
Use Cache::remember() for expensive queries. Add database indexes on columns used in WHERE, ORDER BY, and JOIN clauses.
Never put business logic in Blade templates or controllers. Use services for logic, resources for response shaping.

pattern.name: Eloquent Model
pattern.description: Model with fillable, casts, typed relationships, scopes, and SoftDeletes.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

class Post extends Model
{
    use HasFactory, SoftDeletes;

    protected $fillable = [
        'title', 'slug', 'body', 'status', 'user_id',
    ];

    protected $casts = [
        'published_at' => 'datetime',
        'is_featured'  => 'boolean',
    ];

    public function author(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'user_id');
    }

    public function comments(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Comment::class);
    }

    public function scopePublished($query)
    {
        return $query->where('status', 'published')
                     ->whereNotNull('published_at');
    }
}

pattern.name: Thin Controller
pattern.description: API controller that delegates to a service. Uses Form Request, API Resource, and Policy authorization.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Http\Requests\StorePostRequest;
use App\Http\Resources\PostResource;
use App\Models\Post;
use App\Services\PostService;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly PostService $postService,
    ) {}

    public function index(): PostResource
    {
        return PostResource::collection(
            Post::with('author')->published()->paginate(15)
        );
    }

    public function store(StorePostRequest $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $post = $this->postService->create($request->validated());
        return PostResource::make($post)->response()->setStatusCode(201);
    }

    public function show(Post $post): PostResource
    {
        return PostResource::make($post->load('author', 'comments'));
    }

    public function destroy(Post $post): JsonResponse
    {
        $this->authorize('delete', $post);
        $this->postService->delete($post);
        return response()->json(null, 204);
    }
}

pattern.name: Form Request Validation
pattern.description: Validation and authorization in a dedicated FormRequest class.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Http\Requests;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;

class StorePostRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public function authorize(): bool
    {
        return $this->user()->can('create', Post::class);
    }

    /** @return array<string, mixed> */
    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'title'  => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
            'slug'   => ['required', 'string', 'max:255', Rule::unique('posts')],
            'body'   => ['required', 'string', 'min:10'],
            'status' => ['required', Rule::in(['draft', 'published'])],
        ];
    }
}

pattern.name: Migration
pattern.description: Anonymous migration class with up() and down(). Indexes on query columns.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('posts', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->foreignId('user_id')->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->string('title');
            $table->string('slug')->unique();
            $table->text('body');
            $table->string('status')->default('draft');
            $table->timestamp('published_at')->nullable();
            $table->timestamps();
            $table->softDeletes();
            $table->index(['status', 'published_at']);
        });
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        Schema::dropIfExists('posts');
    }
};

pattern.name: Middleware
pattern.description: Custom middleware registered with an alias in bootstrap/app.php (Laravel 11).
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class EnsureUserHasRole
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next, string $role): Response
    {
        if ($request->user()?->role !== $role) {
            abort(403, "Role '{$role}' is required.");
        }
        return $next($request);
    }
}

// Register in bootstrap/app.php (Laravel 11+):
// ->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware) {
//     $middleware->alias(['role' => EnsureUserHasRole::class]);
// })

pattern.name: Feature Test
pattern.description: HTTP integration test using RefreshDatabase, model factories, and actingAs.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Feature;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Tests\TestCase;

class PostControllerTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    public function test_authenticated_user_can_create_post(): void
    {
        $user = User::factory()->create();

        $response = $this->actingAs($user)
            ->postJson('/api/v1/posts', [
                'title'  => 'My Post',
                'slug'   => 'my-post',
                'body'   => 'Post content here.',
                'status' => 'draft',
            ]);

        $response->assertCreated()
                 ->assertJsonPath('data.title', 'My Post');
        $this->assertDatabaseHas('posts', ['slug' => 'my-post']);
    }

    public function test_guest_cannot_create_post(): void
    {
        $this->postJson('/api/v1/posts', ['title' => 'My Post'])
             ->assertUnauthorized();
    }
}

routing.description: Web routes use middleware groups; API routes are versioned under /api/v1/ with Sanctum auth.

rules.rule: Use apiResource for API controllers (excludes create/edit view routes)
Use route model binding for automatic model resolution
Name routes explicitly when referenced in code: ->name('posts.publish')

quick-reference.item: Form Request classes — never validate in controllers
Queue anything over 200ms: email, PDF, notifications
Always include down(); never modify deployed migrations
Enabled by default on web routes — never disable globally
